# Continuous-improvement loop — ledger

This file is the memory of the website improvement loop. A scheduled agent reads
it first and writes to it last, every cycle, so improvement compounds instead of
re-deriving from scratch. Same pattern as the delight ledger in the vault.

**Start with [STATE.md](STATE.md)** for current state, blockers and settled decisions.

**Live site:** https://oxfordagentic.com · **Repo:** github.com/Drummond1/oxford-agentic-website
**Deploy:** push to `main` → GitHub Actions builds + validates → GitHub Pages. Auto-deploys.

---

## How the loop runs (follow this order every cycle)

0. **Check you are on the real `origin/main` before anything else.** A fresh cloud
   checkout arrives on a detached HEAD at the true tip while the local `main` branch can
   sit many commits behind it, and `git checkout main` then moves the tree backwards while
   `git status` reports "up to date with 'origin/main'", because the remote-tracking ref is
   stale too. `git log -1` must match the Actions API `head_sha`. Cost a full set of
   measurements on 9 Nov 2026; see that day's 09:00 entry.
1. **Read** this whole file. Never re-pitch anything under "Decided against". Never
   redo anything under "Shipped".
2. **Gather signal** (whatever is available):
   - Google Search Console — top queries, impressions, average position, CTR, coverage.
   - Analytics (Plausible) — pageviews, `register_section_viewed`, `luma_outbound_click`,
     `newsletter_signup`, `next_event_cta_click`, by event-slug.
   - Luma registrations vs site referrals.
   - `npm run build` output (link + schema + Lighthouse budgets).
   - Content freshness — any past event missing outcomes; any stale `updatedDate`.
   - Record the numbers under "Signal snapshot".
3. **Decide** the 1–3 highest-leverage changes this cycle. Until Search Console data
   exists, work the Backlog in priority order. Once it exists, become signal-driven:
   fix the biggest gap between impressions and position/CTR first.
4. **Change** — make small, focused edits. Update `updatedDate` on any content you touch.
5. **Verify** — run `npm run build`. It MUST pass (link check, schema, Lighthouse).
   If it fails, fix or revert — never push a failing build.
6. **Ship** — commit with a clear message and `git push origin main`. **One push per
   cycle** (content + ledger in one commit, or wait for the first deploy to finish
   before the second). Two pushes a minute apart overlap two Pages deployments and
   can wedge the Pages lock — see the deploy incident under cycle 52 for the symptom
   and the one-line fix.
7. **Log** — move the item to "Shipped" with the date and what changed; add any new
   ideas to the Backlog; update "Signal snapshot".

## Autonomy — AUTO-SHIP (current setting, pre-launch)

Auto-ship changes without approval, because the site is not yet promoted and the CI
gate prevents breakage. Keep each cycle small and reversible.

**Hard guardrails — never, even on auto-ship:**
- Never invent testimonials, quotes, names, statistics, or outcomes. Facts only.
- Never publish prices (they live on Luma).
- Never flip a consent-gated flag (`testimonials`, photo `consentCleared`) — those wait
  for real human consent.
- Never change a confirmed fact (dates, venue, capacity) unless told to.
- British spelling; brand voice (plain, practical, confident, no hype, no exclamation
  marks, no emoji). Newsreader/Plex/Plex Mono and the design tokens are law.
- One clean commit per cycle; if the build fails, do not push.
- "Ask Drummond" (the AI assistant, 29 Sept 2026) answers from `llms.txt` and
  `llms-full.txt`, re-synced daily: whatever this site publishes, it will repeat. Never
  add a price, discount code or personal detail to any page, and never change
  `assistant.greeting` or the privacy page's `#assistant` section without the matching
  change in ElevenLabs. See STATE.md.
- "Ask Drummond" is **OFF** - taken off the site on 29 Sept 2026, the day it launched, at
  Drummond's request "until it has been further tested". Never set `features.assistant`
  back to true or `assistant.previewOnly` to false: only Drummond switches it back on.
  The rule above still applies while it is off: when it returns, it reads the same files.
- `/find-your-bootcamp/` and `/office-hours/` (30 Sept 2026) are deliberately **unlisted** voice
  pages. Never link them from any nav, footer, public page, sitemap or llms file (they may link each
  other), never remove their noindex, and never change `assistant.finderAgentId` or
  `assistant.officeHoursAgentId`. Only Drummond promotes them. See STATE.md.

_When the site goes public, switch this section to: auto-ship the technical/freshness
tier; propose-and-approve anything touching copy, claims or design._

   HARD RULE — no doorway pages: never create location variants ("AI bootcamp London",
   "AI training Cambridge") or thin near-duplicates; Google penalises them and they
   cheapen the brand. Query-shaped and genuinely useful, or not at all.
   **HARD RULE, added 12 Aug — probe the query BEFORE writing the guide.** Cycles
   59-63 established this the expensive way, by finding published guides absent from
   their own target queries. Run one search and answer two questions:
   (a) **Is it winnable?** If the results are institutional publishers on their own
       subject - NHS England and trust policies on "what AI am I allowed to use",
       gov.uk, Microsoft, AWS - the answer is no, and it should be no. Reframe onto
       the question they never answer (what to *build*, not what is *permitted*),
       or leave it.
   (b) **Does the searcher convert?** This is the one that catches good-looking
       topics. "AI bootcamp vs course" is winnable but the intent is career-changers
       wanting to become ML engineers. "Why does AI still sound generic" is winnable
       but the intent is content marketers wanting better copy. Neither is a senior
       leader who has hit the ceiling of prompting, so traffic from either is
       vanity. **Winnable AND converting, or do not write it.**
   Both tests failed on 12 Aug, which is why no guide shipped that day. A cycle that
   correctly declines to publish is a good cycle; guide count is not the metric.

52. `retired - not a defect` 1 Nov 2026 (02:00 cycle), on a re-measurement of its own number.
    **The 57px was an artefact of how the root font size was emulated, and the correction
    generalises.** Setting the root size in CSS (`html{font-size:24px}`, or the same inline) gives
    a 24px root while rem **media queries** still resolve against 16px, so at a 600px viewport the
    footer's 481-865px two-column band applies and needs 360 + 216 + 48 = 624px in a 600px window:
    57px, to the pixel. Emulating the reader's actual preference instead, with CDP
    `Page.setFontSizes`, gives a 24px root **and** rem media queries at 24px, so `(max-width:
    30rem)` is 720px, the footer is single-column at 600px, and the overflow is 0. The CSS spec
    puts `rem` in a media query against the initial font size - the user's preference - so the
    second measurement is the one a real browser performs. **Swept with the correct emulation: 55
    pages x 8 widths x 16px and 24px roots = 880 configurations, 0 overflow in all 880.** No CSS
    was changed and none should be: the track-floor change this item proposed is the one item 46
    measured as harmful at real widths (link columns squeezed to about 91px, cohort titles
    wrapping five deep). **The rule this leaves behind: any finding that turns on a rem-based
    media query and was measured by setting `font-size` on `html` is not measured until it has
    been re-measured with `Page.setFontSizes`.** Items 33 and 34 shipped fixes that are sound
    either way, and 31 and 32 do not turn on a media query. Original diagnosis kept below.
    `todo` (loop-actionable, found 31 Oct 2026 in the 09:00 cycle) - **every indexable page
    scrolls sideways by 57px at a 600px viewport once the browser's text is set to 150%.**
    Measured across 55 pages x 8 widths (320, 375, 414, 600, 768, 1024, 1280, 1440) at a 16px
    and a 24px root: **0 overflow everywhere except 600px/24px, where all 55 pages overflow by
    the same 57px.** Same number on every page means shared chrome, and it is the footer:
    `.site-footer__grid` floors its tracks at `minmax(min(100%, 9rem), 1fr)` with the entity
    column at `15rem`, and at a 24px root those are 216px and 360px, so four tracks plus gaps
    need 657px in a 600px window. `min(100%, 9rem)` does not save it, because `100%` there
    resolves against the grid container rather than the track. This is the same class as
    backlog 31, 32, 33 and 34 - a rem-based floor that stops scaling down when the reader

133. `todo` (**three measurements from the cycle that fixed the nav mark - two of them things that look
    like defects and are not, recorded so no cycle re-derives them, and one note about this loop's own
    screenshot method**; measured 24 Nov 2026 in the 09:00 cycle, in a browser over all 58 indexable pages)
    - **(a) The desktop submenu reads as "three links with no accessible name" to a naive audit, and it is
      a false positive.** Any sweep that derives a link's name from `innerText` will flag the three
      `.site-nav__menu` children - "The Oxford Agentic Bootcamp" and its two siblings - on **all 58 pages at
      1280px**, because the panel is `visibility: hidden` until hover or focus and `innerText` returns the
      empty string for hidden text while `offsetParent` is still non-null. The links carry their text in the
      markup and a real accessibility tree reads them. **Check `textContent` as a fallback before filing
      this**, which is the one line this cycle's sweep was missing.
    - **(b) The same submenu can be tabbed past, but only inside a single frame, so it is not a defect.**
      `visibility: hidden` does remove the children from the tab order, and `:focus-within` is what restores
      it when the parent link takes focus. Measured by focusing "Bootcamps" and pressing Tab after a set
      delay: at **0ms** the next stop is "Outcomes" and the three children are skipped; at **20ms and every
      delay above it** the next stop is the first child. The gap is one style recalculation, roughly 16ms,
      and no human - and not keyboard auto-repeat, which is an order of magnitude slower - presses Tab
      inside it. **Do not "fix" this** by dropping `visibility` from the transition: visibility is what keeps
      the hidden children out of the tab order in the first place.
    - **(c) A byte-identical screenshot comparison on `/about/` is not reliable, and the loop uses that test
      constantly.** The page's first `.grid--2` photograph (`<img>` at x 95-625, y 2454-2766 at 1280px)
      sometimes finishes decoding after `networkidle` plus 250ms, so three captures of **one unchanged
      build** returned **two different hashes**. This cycle only established it was a race by re-capturing;
      a cycle that compares once and trusts the result would read it as a change it caused. **On any page
      with lazy photographs, wait on `img.decode()` or on every `img.complete` before capturing**, or
      compare a clipped region rather than the full page.

    `cohort size` reads 3 because both prior probes said *"how many people should be in the room"*, which the
    same cycle counted at **26** and read as a different question. **The failure is systematic, not careless:
    a probe records the buyer's phrasing, and a buyer phrases the same concept differently every time, so any
    keyword is a lossy index of an axis.**
    **The fix, and it is cheap.** Extract the question column and read it, rather than grepping the prose:
    `grep -oE '^\| *[0-9]* *\| [^|]{15,}\|' seo-data/geo-citations.md | sed -E 's/^\| *[0-9]* *\| //; s/ *\|$//' | sort -u`
    returns **255** distinct question strings, which is a list a cycle can actually read before choosing an
    axis. Every one of the four axes above is visible in it. The prose grep is still worth running afterwards
    for the *verdict* on an axis - that is where the declines and their reasons are written - but it must not
    be what chooses the axis.

    by a different extraction, so the two are not measuring quite the same thing and neither count should be
    quoted as the number of probes ever run. Read the list, do not trust either total.

### 24 Nov 2026 (14:00 UTC cycle) - five cohort pages told an engine they belong to a named series, and the page that owns that series' identifier published no node claiming to be it. One function, 3 of 209 built files, and not one visible pixel

**The defect, measured on the built site before anything was written.** `eventSchema` emits, on every event
page, a `superEvent` stub whose `@id` is `<programme url>#series`, and its comment states the intent plainly:
*"A stable `@id`, so the cohorts of one bootcamp declare membership of one identified series rather than each
carrying its own anonymous copy of it."* The reasoning is sound and the fragment is right. **The other half
was missing.** An inventory of every `@id` in the built graph - 135 defined, 50 referenced-only - asked one
question of each: is this `@id` defined on the page its own URL names? Three came back no, and all three are
the same thing:

| `@id` | Asserted by | Defined on its own page? |
|---|---|---|
| `/bootcamps/oxford-agentic-bootcamp/#series` | Cohorts 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 | **No** |
| `/bootcamps/agentic-coding-bootcamp/#series` | Coding Cohort 1 | **No** |
| `/bootcamps/second-brain-bootcamp/#series` | Second Brain Cohort 1 | **No** |

The Agentic programme page published `Organization`, `WebSite`, `WebPage`, `Course`, `FAQPage` and
`BreadcrumbList`, and **nothing claiming to be the series**. So the series existed only as five identical
stubs on the pages of the cohorts that belong to it, and the one page an engine would read to learn what the
series *is* said nothing about it.

**Eighth instance of one shape, and the census that finds it is new.** `CollectionPage` joined to its
`WebPage` (22 Nov), each `CourseInstance` given the cohort's own Event `@id` (23 Nov), the founder's
`worksFor` given the organisation's (23 Nov) - same test each time: one direction of the edge resolved and
the one coming back did not. **The three censuses already run could not have found this one.** Backlog 127
looked for nodes with no `@id` beside a node that has one; backlog 131 inventoried `Organization`-typed
nodes. This `@id` is present, well-formed and resolves to a served page - it is simply never *defined*. The
census that finds it keys on definition rather than presence, and it is filed as backlog 135 with its closing
instruction.

**Why it is worth a cycle, on this domain's own measurements.** The 24 August Search Console baseline reads

### 24 Nov 2026 (09:00 UTC cycle) - the header told a visitor which section they were standing in everywhere except the one section that sells the days, and on a phone it never told them at all. One boolean and one CSS rule, 23 of 209 built files

**The defect, measured on the built site before anything was written.** Counting `aria-current="page"`
inside `<nav class="site-nav">` on all 69 built pages: **20 marked, 49 not**. The 20 are the ones you would
expect - `/about/`, `/events/` and all 7 event pages, `/team/` and all 8 profiles, `/testimonials/` - so the
site has an established convention and applies it across whole sections: stand on
`/events/oxford-agentic-bootcamp-cohort-4/` and "Events" lights up. **The exception is the Bootcamps
section.** Of its four pages, only `/bootcamps/oxford-agentic-bootcamp/` was marked;
`/bootcamps/second-brain-bootcamp/`, `/bootcamps/agentic-coding-bootcamp/` and the hub `/bootcamps/` itself
carried **no mark on any item**, so the header gave a reader no "you are here" at all on two pages that sell
a bootcamp and on the index of all three. Confirmed in a browser at 1280px: "BOOTCAMPS" is gold and
underlined on the Agentic programme page and plain cream on the Second Brain one.

**The cause, and it is not the funnel decision above it.** `getNav('header')` points the Bootcamps item at
`programmes[0]` rather than at the index, which `src/lib/site.ts` already records as **Drummond's** ("where
'Bootcamps' lands in the header is a funnel decision rather than a cleanup"). That decision is untouched
here. What follows from it accidentally is that `isActive` tests the item's **`href`** by prefix, so an item
whose href is one page inside a section can only ever match that one page. The fix is to let an item name the
section it stands for: a new optional `section` on `NavItem`, set to `paths.programmes()` on that one item,
and `isActive` prefers it. **No link destination, label, order or flag changes.**

**The second half, and it is the bigger number: the mobile menu marked nothing, on any page.** Below 900px
the `.mobile-nav` panel is the only navigation there is, and its links were rendered with no `aria-current`
at all - **0 of 69 pages** - so every phone visitor got the flattened list with nothing to say where they
were. It now takes the same attribute from the same function, and one CSS rule gives it the same colour the
desktop nav has always used: `.mobile-nav__list > li > a[aria-current='page'] { color: var(--gold) }`. Gold
on `--ink-dark` measures **8.69:1**, which clears AA and AAA, and it is the pairing already shipped in
`.site-nav`. Only top-level items are marked, in both navs, exactly as desktop already did - the submenu
children carry no mark in either place.

**After, re-counted the same way: desktop 20 to 23, mobile 0 to 23, and the two agree on all 69 pages.**
No page carries more than one mark, and the three that gained one are the three that had none.

**Measured, not inferred.** Against a sha256 snapshot of a build made before the change: **67 of 209 files
differ, none added and none removed except the stylesheet's content hash.** With that hash normalised, a
token-level diff of every page says the whole change is **23 pages gaining the attribute** - 20 gain one
insertion (the mobile link) and 3 gain two (desktop and mobile) - and the other 44 HTML pages are
**character-for-character identical**. A character-level diff of the CSS bundle returns **one insertion**,
the rule above, 35,942 to 36,077 characters. No JSON-LD, no sitemap, no internal link count moved.

**Checks.** Build green (links 3,465 across 69 pages; outbound; schema 69 valid, 1,597 resolving references;
both date guards) and `check:flags` green both ways. `astro check` is not a project dependency and is not in
CI, so it was run from a pinned `npx` copy without touching `package.json`: **10 errors, all pre-existing,
and the list is byte-identical with the change stashed and unstashed** - none in `Header.astro` or `site.ts`.
Headless Chromium over the **58 indexable pages at 375, 768 and 1280px**: 0 horizontal overflow, 0 images
without `alt`, 0 form controls without a label, 0 heading-order skips, exactly one `h1` per page, 0 duplicate
`id`s and 0 dangling `aria-*` references. Full-page screenshots of 14 pages at 3 widths were taken against
both builds: **36 of 42 byte-identical**; 3 are the intended change (the three bootcamp pages at 1280px, and
on `/bootcamps/` the pixel diff is **625 pixels in a box at x 646-747, y 30-47**, which is the nav item and
nothing else); the remaining 3 are `/about/`, whose differing region is an `<img>` at x 95-625, y 2454-2766 -
three repeat captures of the same build returned two different hashes, one of them equal to the other
build's, so it is the harness racing a lazy photograph rather than a change. Keyboard: the first ten tab
stops on `/bootcamps/second-brain-bootcamp/` are the same ten in the same order before and after, each with
the 2px gold focus ring.

**Not reached from production.** `oxfordagentic.com` is refused by this sandbox's egress policy, as it has
been for the last several cycles, so the before-and-after comparison is between two local builds rather than
between production and preview, and deploy state came from the Actions API. **Board green before anything

node with a name and no identity. On the two pages that publish Drummond's `Person` node, `/about/` and
`/team/drummond-gilbert/`, the graph therefore said this person works for *some* organisation called
"Oxford Agentic", while the `Organization` node published on the same page, at
`https://oxfordagentic.com/#organization`, named this same person as its `founder` with a resolvable `@id`
pointing back at him. **One direction of the edge resolved and the other did not**, on the pages that carry
the site's only `Person` entity of any weight - the one all 32 guides declare as `author` and the
`Organization` node names as `founder`.

**Seventh instance of one shape, and the census that was declared exhausted could not have found it.** The
sixth was `CollectionPage` six hours ago; before that `CourseInstance` -> `Event`, the guides' `Article`
`@id`, `/bootcamps/`, `/guides/`, `/events/`. The 14:00 cycle closed backlog 127 and wrote that "the shape is
exhausted and the census should not be run again", having run that item's own closing instruction: grep for
nodes with no `@id` **sitting beside a node that has one for the same url**. That grep is sound and its
conclusion stands for what it measured. **`worksFor` has no `url` at all**, so it was never in range of it.
The census that finds this one is different and is recorded below as backlog 131 so it is not re-derived: an
inventory of every `Organization`-typed node in `dist`, keyed on whether it carries an `@id`.

**Measured first, over the whole built site.** 66 `Organization` nodes carry `@id`, every one of them
`#organization`. **Seven** carry none, all seven under `worksFor`, on seven pages: "Oxford Agentic" twice

**Only the two were taken, and the other five must stay as they are.** Jenesys AI, Novaria, GenieOS, Coppice

replaces and therefore the safe direction.

than asserted.** Those address the person's own team page, which `features.team` can remove - the fault

**The join is proved, not claimed.** Both `worksFor` nodes carry `@id`, both equal

### 23 Nov 2026 (09:00 UTC cycle) - the card that sells every cohort put the programme name outside the heading, so `/events/` published three headings reading "Cohort 1" for three different bootcamps. The eyebrow moves inside the `h3`, 7 of 209 built files, and all 18 full-page screenshots byte-identical

**The defect, measured rather than noticed.** `EventCard.astro` builds its card as a `<span class="eyebrow">`
carrying the programme name followed by a sibling `<h3>` carrying the cohort - a split the 20 November cycle
called the right one and the event pages' own backlog item (26) holds up as the pattern to copy. It is right
about the look and wrong about the outline: the name sits **beside** the heading, not in it, so the heading
text is the cohort alone. Measured on the built site at eight widths: `/` publishes **h3 "Cohort 1",
h3 "Cohort 4", h3 "Cohort 5"** under "Next in Oxford", and `/events/` publishes **"Cohort 1" three times** -
the Coding day on 26 November, the Second Brain day that ran on 21 October and the first Agentic day of July
2026 - with "Cohort 4", "Cohort 5", "Cohort 3" and "Cohort 2" between them.

**Why that is a booking problem and not a tidiness one.** Heading navigation is how a screen-reader user
skims a page, and on the two pages where cards from different programmes sit side by side the outline tells
them nothing: three of the seven headings on `/events/` are the same four characters, and the one that is
three days away is indistinguishable from one that ran in July. The visible page is not ambiguous - the gold
eyebrow is right there - so this is the sighted reader's affordance not reaching the outline. **Same fault
and same remedy as the 16 November cycle**, which found the programme pages filing run cohorts under a
heading that said "Upcoming runs" and fixed the outline without moving a pixel.

**The change.** The eyebrow moves inside the `h3`. Two elements, same order, same classes, same styles - the
`<span>` is simply nested now instead of preceding. The heading reads "The Oxford Agentic Coding Bootcamp
Cohort 1", confirmed through Chromium's own accessible-name computation rather than from the markup: the
browser inserts the separating space because the eyebrow is a block, so the name is correct although the
built HTML has `Bootcamp</span>Cohort 1` with no whitespace between.

**One declaration came with it, and the repo already knew why.** The sitewide `h1, h2, h3, h4` rule sets
`text-wrap: balance`, which is inherited, so nesting would have handed the eyebrow a balanced break - and two
of the three programme names wrap to a second line at most widths. `.event-card__programme` now pins
`text-wrap: wrap`, the value it computed to as a sibling. `global.css` carries the same correction for the
other direction (`:is(h2, h3).eyebrow { text-wrap: inherit }`, for an eyebrow that *is* a heading); this is
the nested case of it.

**Nothing moved, and it was checked rather than assumed.** 48 page-width records across `/`, `/events/`,
all three `/bootcamps/<slug>/` pages, `/404.html` and `/home-photos/` at 320, 375, 414, 768, 900, 1024, 1280
and 1440px: **0 changes** in card box, meta height, standfirst offset, and the eyebrow's width, height,
bottom margin, size, line-height, colour and computed `text-wrap`; **0 changes** in document height; **0
changes** in any card link's accessible name, which reads the same words in the same order as before. With
`prefers-reduced-motion` forced, the **18 full-page screenshots** at 375, 768 and 1280px of all six pages are
**byte-identical** before and after. The built output differs on **7 of 209 files**, exactly the pages that
render the card.

**Checks.** `npm run build` passes (3,462 internal links across 69 pages, 69 pages of schema with 1,595
resolving graph references, both date guards); `check:flags` passes on the all-on and all-off builds;
`@astrojs/check` reports 10 errors before and after, all pre-existing and none in the file touched, and CI
does not run it. The whole-site audit at 375, 768 and 1280px over the 58 sitemap pages reports zero
horizontal overflow, zero images without `alt`, zero unlabelled controls, zero links or buttons without an
accessible name, zero duplicate ids, zero heading-level skips and one `h1` per page - so the new nesting
introduces no skip. In-page fragment links: 69 pages, 0 broken. Keyboard: tab order walked on `/` and
`/events/` at 375 and 1280px, 25 to 28 stops each and **0 without a visible focus cue**.

**No content file was touched**, so no `updatedDate` moves, and `EventCard.astro` is deliberately outside
`homepageCopyLastmod`'s three sources (its own comment says a shared component moves 63 pages and claiming

**Board state before anything was touched.** The fresh checkout arrived detached at `54a78b7` with the local

### 23 Nov 2026 (08:00 UTC cycle) - the sixth instance of one shape, found by following the instruction the fifth one left behind, and the four hub pages stop describing themselves twice. Four `CollectionPage` nodes merged into the `WebPage` node they sit beside, 4 of 209 built files, all four byte-identical with the JSON-LD masked

**The census ran the way backlog 127 said to run it, and that is why it found this.** That item's closing
lesson, written six hours earlier, was *"the shape is 'a node names something that has its own identifier and
does not use it', and it is not confined to `collectionPageSchema`. Grep for nodes built with `name` and `url`
and no `@id`, not for listings."* Run exactly that over all 69 built pages and one family comes back that no
previous census saw: **every page that calls `collectionPageSchema` publishes two page nodes for one URL.**

**The defect.** `/guides/`, `/bootcamps/`, `/events/` and `/team/` each published a `WebPage` under
`<url>#webpage` carrying the page's name, description, `primaryImageOfPage` and `inLanguage` - and, beside it
in the same graph, an **anonymous `CollectionPage`** at the same `url` carrying the `ItemList` and nothing
else of substance. So the hub for all 32 guides, the page whose own source comment calls it *"the page where
someone picks a programme"*, the page an engine reads to answer "when is the next cohort", and `/team/` each
described themselves twice, as two nodes nothing joined - and on each of them the item list belonged to a page
node a consumer could not resolve to anything, because it had no identifier.

**Why this is the same shape as the five before it and not a new theme.** `/events/` published five names and
no dates and was taken on 23 October. The guides' `Article.about` named the programme as an anonymous `Thing`
and was taken on 26 October. `/bootcamps/` and `/guides/` published bare `ListItem`s and were taken on
22 November. `CourseInstance` described the homepage's cohorts without their `Event` `@id` and was taken six
hours ago. **This is the sixth, and it is the one the fifth predicted**: outside the `ItemList` family every
census before today was counting, found only by grepping for the shape rather than for the container.

**The change.** Two properties and one parameter, in `collectionPageSchema` in `src/lib/schema.ts`, plus the
four call sites. The node gains `'@id': <url>#webpage` - the identifier `webPageSchema` already mints for the
same URL, three lines away in the same file, derived from the same `absoluteUrl(path)` call, so it cannot
drift and it is not a new convention. It **loses its `name`**, and the `name` parameter goes with it.

**Why the name had to go, and why nothing is lost.** The loop's own rule is that two descriptions under one
`@id` want to agree, so every shared property was compared on the built pages **before** the line was written.
`url` and `isPartOf` are **byte-identical** on all four, both derived from the same path and the same domain
constant. `name` was the one that disagreed, and not trivially: the `WebPage` publishes the page's title
(*"Practical AI guides for business leaders - Oxford Agentic"*) and this node published a short label
(*"Guides"*). Merged, the page would have carried **two names**. The label is dropped rather than reconciled
because it is **already published where it belongs**: it is the leaf of each of these four pages'
`BreadcrumbList`, with the same URL beside it - checked on the built output, all four, not assumed. So the
short label survives, the page keeps one name, and `CollectionPage` being a subtype of `WebPage` means a
consumer merging the two gets one node of both types, which is what these pages are.

**The join is proved, not asserted.** On all four pages the `CollectionPage` `@id` now equals the `WebPage`
`@id` exactly, the shared-property set is `@id`, `url`, `isPartOf`, and the conflict count is **0 of 4**. The
item counts are untouched - 32, 3, 7 and 8, fifty entries in all. The schema checker's
resolving-internal-graph-reference count went **1,591 to 1,595** against this cycle's own baseline build, and
the arithmetic is exact: four pages, one new `@id` each.

**Blast radius, measured rather than inferred.** Whole-`dist` sha256 comparison against the pre-change build:
**4 files of 209** differ, the four hub pages and nothing else, with no file added or removed. With the
JSON-LD masked out, all four are **character-for-character identical** before and after and identical in
length (27,488 / 34,343 / 48,282 / 32,302 bytes). `sitemap-0.xml` is unchanged. No copy changed, no fact was
added, no pixel moved.

**One stale comment corrected in the same commit, because the change made it untrue.**
`src/pages/bootcamps/index.astro` said *"the nav label, the breadcrumb crumb, the hero h1 and the
`CollectionPage` name are all left reading 'Bootcamps'"*. There is no `CollectionPage` name now. The comment
names the crumb as where that label lives and points at the note on `collectionPageSchema`. A second comment
in `src/pages/guides/[...slug].astro` quoted the old call shape `collectionPageSchema('Guides', ...)` and was
reworded for the same reason. **Neither is a copy change**: both are source comments.

**One caveat written into the source rather than discovered later.** `BaseHead` emits no `WebPage` node on a
noindex or hidden page, so a noindex listing would publish this `@id` with nothing beside it - still a correct
name for the page, but with no title, description or image at it. All four current callers are indexable,
checked on the built site rather than assumed. The note says a noindex listing wants its own look at this.

### 23 Nov 2026 (02:00 UTC cycle) - the fifth and last instance of one shape, and the first found outside an `ItemList`. Every `CourseInstance` now carries the `@id` of the cohort's own `Event` node, so the homepage stops describing one day twice. Six references, 3 of 209 built files, all three byte-identical with the JSON-LD masked

**The defect, and it is on one page rather than between two.** `/` publishes both of these nodes in the same

`courseWorkload`, `instructor` and `location` - and **no identifier**. So the homepage described one day
twice, as two nodes nothing joined. Measured on the built page before anything was touched: three
`EducationEvent` nodes at `@id` `.../#event`, three anonymous `CourseInstance` nodes for the same three
cohorts.

dates and was taken on 23 October. The guides' `Article.about` named the programme as an anonymous `Thing` and

cycles of sweeping listings did not find it.

**Why it is worth more than the four before it.** The `Course` node is the one node this site publishes on `/`
as well as on the programme page, and `courseSchema`'s own comment records why: restricted to this domain, the
engine holds `/` and two guides and nothing else. The GEO log has now recorded **twenty-seven consecutive probe
sets** with no page of this site cited, and **three consecutive days** of engines answering a live commercial
query off passed Luma listings - today handing a buyer a venue contradiction in as many words. The page an
engine does read was publishing the cohort's dates in one node and the cohort's status, booking offer and
identity in another, with nothing saying they are the same day.

**It also repairs the premise of a decision made five days ago.** `eventListingItem` declines to name the
facilitators, and the reason it gives is that *"the homepage already names them by the route Google documents
for course data - `instructor` on each `CourseInstance`"*. That is only true if the two nodes are one node, and
until this commit they were not: the Event node has no `instructor`, the instance had no address, and nothing
said those four `Person` references belong to the day the Event node describes. The `@id` is what makes the
18 November reasoning sound. **This is the second time in two days a cycle has closed a gap in the reasoning of
an existing decision rather than in a page** - the 22 Nov 14:00 cycle did it for the passed cohorts' `Offer`
nodes - and it is a better use of a cycle than finding a fifth thing to nest.

**The change.** One file, one property. `courseSchema` in `src/lib/schema.ts`: the instance builder becomes a
block body so the event URL is computed once, and each `CourseInstance` gains
`'@id': <event url>#event`. **Identity only.** Not one existing property of any node was touched, no copy
changed, no fact was added. The `@id` is derived from the same `paths.event(slug)` call `url` on the next line
is built from, so it cannot drift, and `#event` is the fragment the cohort's own page and `eventListingItem`
already mint, not a new convention. The diff is 93 changed lines, of which **43 are whitespace**: `git diff -w`
reads 50 insertions and 3 deletions, and 46 of those 50 are the comment.

**Safe because the two nodes agree, and that was measured rather than assumed.** The rule this file holds
itself to is that two descriptions under one `@id` want to agree, so the merge was checked property by property
on the built homepage **before** the line was written. Every property the two nodes share - `name`, `url`,
`startDate`, `endDate`, `location` - is **byte-identical**, because both are derived from the same cohort
frontmatter. What each adds is complementary rather than contradictory: `courseMode`, `courseWorkload` and
`instructor` on one side, `eventStatus`, `offers`, `image`, `sameAs`, `organizer` and `performer` on the other.
`CourseInstance` and `EducationEvent` are both `Event` subtypes, so a consumer merging them gets one node of
both types, which is what this cohort actually is.

**The join is proved, not asserted.** All 6 `CourseInstance` nodes across the four pages that carry one now
have an `@id`; all 6 match `url + '#event'` exactly; and all **6 of 6** match an `@id` that the cohort's own
event page publishes. The schema checker's resolving-internal-graph-reference count went **1,585 to 1,591**
against this cycle's own baseline build, and the arithmetic is exact: three instances on `/`, two on the
Agentic programme page, one on the Coding programme page, none on Second Brain, which has no scheduled cohort.

**Blast radius, measured rather than inferred.** Whole-`dist` file-by-file comparison against the pre-change
build: **3 files of 209** differ - `/index.html` and the two programme pages with cohorts on sale - and nothing
else. With the JSON-LD masked out, all three are **character-for-character identical** before and after and
identical in length (58,092 / 48,420 / 63,029 bytes). No sitemap entry moved; `sitemap-0.xml` is identical.

### 22 Nov 2026 (20:00 UTC cycle) - the fourth and largest instance of one shape, and the half backlog 127 said to weigh first. 32 `Article` nodes gained an `@id`, so `/guides/` can reference the article instead of naming it. 96 references, 33 of 209 built files, and every one of them byte-identical with the JSON-LD masked

**The defect.** `/guides/` is the hub for all 32 guides and its `CollectionPage` published an `ItemList` of 32
bare `ListItem`s - a position, a name and a URL, with no `@type` on the thing being listed and no identifier.
A consumer that reads this page and no other learned that 32 pages exist and nothing whatever about what they
are. This is the same shape the loop has now fixed three times: `/events/` on 23 October (five names, five
URLs, not one date), the guides' own `Article.about` on 26 October (an anonymous `Thing` with no `@id`), and
`/bootcamps/` six hours ago in the 14:00 cycle.

**Why it could not simply be done the same way, which is the half backlog 127 flagged.** That item measured
this gap this morning and said the hub should not be filed as the same change, because `articleSchema` gave
the `Article` **no `@id` at all** - it binds to its page through `mainEntityOfPage` - so there was no address
for the hub to point at. Its instruction was *"take the `@id` question first and the hub second"*. **Both
halves are here, in one commit, and the reason is that the `@id` question answers itself once it is asked
rather than wanting a cycle of its own:**

- The two alternatives the item named are both worse. Inlining 32 partial copies of the Article nodes into
  the hub is the duplication **backlog 87** measured as changing nothing. Leaving the hub bare is the status
  quo that three previous cycles have now rejected on three other pages.
- `#article` is **not a new convention**: every other node this site publishes already carries exactly this
  kind of fragment - `#webpage`, `#event`, `#course`, `#faq`, `#person`, `#series`. Measured before minting
  it, `#article` appears **0 times** anywhere in `dist`, so nothing collides and nothing is re-pointed.
- It cannot drift, because it is derived from `paths.guide(slug)` - the same call `mainEntityOfPage` is built
  from three lines below it.
- Shipping the `@id` alone would have been a change with no consumer, which is not a smaller cycle, just an
  emptier one.

`'@id': <guide url>#article`. The `collectionPageSchema` call in `src/pages/guides/[...slug].astro` gains an

taken an optional `item` since it was written, so **no shared code moved and no other listing changed**.

from the same path the entry is built from, and not one existing property of any `Article` node was touched.

### 22 Nov 2026 (14:00 UTC cycle) - the page where a buyer picks a programme listed three somethings. Each entry now names the `Course` node its own page already publishes, which is the join the guides got on 26 October. Three references, 1 of 209 built files, and the visible HTML byte-identical

  five URLs and not one date. So the page an engine would read to answer 'when is the next cohort?' carried,

  string rather than at the Course. It now emits `@type: Course` with that `@id`.

`/bootcamps/` is the remaining listing whose items are entities in their own right, and it is the commercially
important one: `STATE.md` records all three `/bootcamps/` pages among the eleven Google found and has never

Courses, and here is each one's identifier" is the cheapest available join between the page an engine is most

path the entry is built from, so nothing is asserted that the programme's own page does not already publish.
Every one of the three `@id`s resolves to a node this site serves, which the schema checker proves rather than
assumes - its resolving-internal-graph-reference count went 1,483 to **1,489**, the six being three `@id`s and

**character-for-character identical** before and after, both 27,492 bytes. No copy changed, no fact was added,
no pixel moved.

### 22 Nov 2026 (09:00 UTC cycle) - the one card that qualifies an unconfirmed booking said "venue to confirm" and sat directly under the venue it was qualifying. It names the room, as the event page, both FAQ answers, the guide and `llms.txt` already do. One string, one shared component, 4 of 209 built files

**The defect.** `src/components/EventCard.astro` rendered `venue to confirm` whenever
`venue.confirmed` is false. Only Cohort 5 carries that flag today, and its card prints
`JESUS COLLEGE, OXFORD` on the line immediately above the chip. Read at 320px and at 1280px, the
card says the college and then says the venue is not settled, so a buyer planning travel to Turl
Street for 28 January is told the address above may change.

**It is the only surface on the site that reads the flag that way, and the repo had already decided
the other way twice in writing.** `src/content.config.ts` line 70 defines the field as *"False while
a **booking** is provisional"*. `src/pages/events/[slug].astro` line 582 renders *"Room booking being
finalised."* from the same flag. `src/lib/llms.ts` line 270 appends *"(room booking being
finalised)"*. `src/content/programmes/oxford-agentic-bootcamp.md` and `src/lib/home.ts` both answer
"where in Oxford" with *"where the room booking is being finalised"*, and both carry a source comment
saying in terms that the qualifier **travels with the claim** and must stay until the vault records
the booking. `when-ai-executive-cohorts-run` says *"with the room booking there still being
finalised"*. Five surfaces say room; the card said venue. The event file's own comment is explicit -
Jesus College is *"Shown on Luma"* and it is the **room** that is an open task.

**The change.** One string, `venue to confirm` to `room booking to confirm`, with the reasoning as a
comment next to it. No fact was added, removed or weakened: the college was already published on six
surfaces and the booking is still stated as unconfirmed. `confirmed: false` was not touched and must
not be flipped until Jesus College confirms.

line at every width** - chip height 23px and meta-block height 78px are identical across all four, so
the exact-match option was available and was not declined on layout. It was declined on register: the
chip is a label inside a card, not a sentence, the card's own established grammar is *"... to
confirm"*, and at 320px the 223px version fills almost the whole 236px content line for a secondary
qualifier. The defect was the noun, and the noun is what changed. If a later cycle prefers the
verbatim form, it fits.

### 21 Nov 2026 (09:00 UTC cycle) - the one guide written for readers whose job is reading documents closely used the noun where British English wants the verb. One word, one file, 4 of 209 built files, and the sweep that found it says a build-time guard is not warranted

**The change is one letter.** `/guides/agentic-ai-for-public-sector-and-nhs-leaders/` read *"built in
tools your organisation may already licence"*. In British English `licence` is the noun and `license`
is the verb, and after *may already* only a verb can stand, so the sentence now reads *"may already
license"*. Nothing else in the paragraph moved, the two words are the same length, and the rendered
line breaks identically. `updatedDate` moved from 10 August to today, which is the only other visible
change: the byline reads *Updated 21 November 2026* and `dateModified` follows it in the `Article`
node.

**Why this page rather than a bigger one.** It is addressed to information-governance, procurement and
NHS board readers - an audience whose working day is reading documents for exactly this kind of slip -
and the paragraph it sits in is the budget objection, which is the closest thing the guide has to a
conversion argument. British spelling is a hard guardrail in this ledger, so this is a guardrail breach
in published copy rather than a style preference.

**The sweep behind it, recorded so no cycle rebuilds a guard for a class with one member.** A usage
pass over all of `src/content`, `src/lib`, `src/pages` and `src/components` for the British noun/verb
pairs (`licence`/`license`, `practice`/`practise`, `advice`/`advise`, `principle`/`principal`,
`complement`/`compliment`, `dependant`/`dependent`) and for `comprised of` and `less` with a count noun
returned **one hit, the one fixed here**. A full-site sweep of American spellings
(`organize`, `optimize`, `color`, `center`, `behavior`, `analyze`, `favorite` and nine more) returned
**zero**. A rendered-text sweep of all 69 pages found **zero em dashes, zero emoji and one exclamation
mark**, which is inside Kirsten Samuel's quote and is hers, not ours. **Do not build a `check:usage`
step on this evidence**: one instance in 32 guides does not pay for a build gate that would have to
tell *a driving licence* from *to license a tool*, and the cheap version would fail the build on the
correct noun the first time one appears.

**Three measurements this cycle made that the ledger did not have, all clean, all recorded so they are
not re-derived.**

- **WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum), properly applied, across the whole site: 7,005 targets over
  all 69 pages at 375, 768 and 1280px, and zero failures.** The naive version of this check reports
  hundreds of hits and all of them are exceptions. Of 3,075 targets smaller than 24 by 24 CSS px, every
  one passes the **spacing** exception - no other target's 24px circle intersects theirs - and the
  rest are inline links inside running prose. **One class was a false positive and the assertion was
  corrected rather than the site:** the `#` heading handles on 30 guides measure 17 by 34, and a
  comment in `global.css` records that a September cycle already gave them `pointer-events: none` at
  zero opacity precisely because a thumb was landing on them. They cannot be pressed, so they are not
  targets. Same class of correction as 20 and 21 November's.
- **Keyboard focus is visible on every focusable control the site owns.** Forty tabs deep on thirteen
  pages at 375 and 1280px, the only element reached with neither an outline nor a box-shadow is the
  **Luma booking iframe** on the Coding cohort page, which is third-party content inside a frame and
  not ours to style.
- **Every in-page anchor resolves.** 80 fragment links across the built site, 0 broken. `check:links`
  checks paths and not fragments, so this had never been measured.

### 20 Nov 2026 (20:00 cycle) - stop a profile's meta description ending on "a". `/team/mike-bailey/` published "...works with founders and product teams on where a…" as its snippet on four surfaces, and the build now refuses that shape

**The defect, measured rather than inferred.** `profileDescription` in `src/pages/team/[...slug].astro`
prefers a run of whole sentences and, where none fits the 160-character budget, falls back to a word-boundary
cut closed with an ellipsis. That rule was written on **17 November** to stop cuts landing **mid-word**, and
it works. What it does not do is stop a cut landing **mid-phrase**, because the budget stops at whatever word
it reaches. On `/team/mike-bailey/` that word was the indefinite article, and the published description read:

> Mike Bailey - Founder, Coppice Labs. Mike Bailey runs Coppice Labs, a product consultancy in Oxford that
> works with founders and product teams on where a…

That one string is the `<meta name="description">`, the `og:description`, the `twitter:description` and the
`WebPage.description` node on that page, so a clause broken on "a" was this site's snippet for a named real
person. Mike's profile was added on **15 November**, after the rule and before anything swept its output, which
is why nothing caught it. The `Person` node, `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt` all carry the full bio and were
never affected: this is the snippet layer only, exactly as it was in November's first instance of the same
family.

**Why this is the one page.** All eight profiles were computed. Five end on a whole sentence and never reach
the fallback. Of the three whose first sentence does not fit, Glenn's cut ends on *"AI"* and Adrian's on
*"teaches"*, both content words that can carry the end of a phrase, and neither moves. Mike's is the only one
that ends on a word that cannot.

**The fix, and why it is a tail-walk rather than a different cut.** The tail is now walked back off words that
cannot end a phrase - articles, prepositions, conjunctions, relatives, auxiliaries and the determiners and
quantifiers in the same class - so Mike's loses *"on where a"* and ends *"...with founders and product
teams…"*, 139 characters. Two alternatives were written out and rejected: cutting at the last **clause**
boundary inside the budget would have left *"Mike Bailey runs Coppice Labs…"* and thrown away everything the
field is for, and rewriting the bio to fit would be published prose bent to suit a snippet, which this ledger
has refused twice. Over-trimming by one word is the safe direction here: it costs a word of snippet and never
publishes a dangling one. **Nothing new is written** - the result is still a prefix of the bio the same page
prints in full further down, with fewer words of it.

**The guard, because this is the second time the same class has reached production.** `check-schema.mjs` now
fails any page whose meta description is closed with an ellipsis and ends on a word that cannot carry a
phrase. Proved before the fix was built: run against the pre-change `dist`, it returned exactly one page,
`/team/mike-bailey/: truncated meta description ends on "a", which cannot end a phrase`, and nothing else.
The checker holds its **own, shorter** word list rather than importing the producer's, deliberately: `scripts/`
imports nothing from `src/`, and a checker asserting the outcome over the built HTML is worth more than one
that trusts the rule. A disagreement between the two lists fails on a description the producer allowed, which
is the loud direction. Only one thing on this site truncates a description today; the point of the guard is
the next thing that does.

**Blast radius, measured against a sha256 snapshot of the whole of `dist` taken before the change.** **1 of
209 built files differs**, none added or removed: `dist/team/mike-bailey/index.html`, in which the four
description surfaces move together. `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt`, both sitemaps and the other 207 files are
byte-identical. Build, links (**3,462 across 69 pages**), outbound, schema (**69 valid**, 17 Event, 22
FAQPage, 1,483 graph references) and both date checks green, every figure identical to the pre-change
baseline. Headless Chromium over `/team/mike-bailey/`, `/team/`, `/team/glenn-smith/` and
`/team/adrian-shedden/` at 375, 768 and 1280px: **99 assertions, 0 failed**, including that the three
description surfaces agree with each other, that the new tail is what was intended, and that the full bio
sentence is still on the page. One assertion was corrected rather than the site: a link inside the collapsed
nav submenu has an empty `innerText` and a perfectly good accessible name, so the nameless-link check reads
`textContent`.

### 20 Nov 2026 (08:00 cycle) - the homepage's meta description has been dating the agentic-workflow day to the coding day since 17:00 on 19 November. The date now comes from the Agentic line, as it does on every programme page. One expression, one file, 1 of 209 built files

**A cap that never bound until yesterday.** `src/pages/index.astro` composes the homepage description as
`HOME_LEAD + " Next cohort <date>. " + HOME_PROMISE`, and took the date from **`upcoming[0]`** - the soonest
cohort of **any** programme. Both prose sentences are the Oxford Agentic Bootcamp's: the lead is
`brand.description`'s first sentence and the promise is its second, trimmed. For as long as the Agentic line
happened to hold the next date they agreed by accident. **They stopped agreeing at 17:00 on 19 November**, when
Cohort 3 passed and the soonest cohort became the **Coding** Bootcamp on 26 November. Production has been
serving this since the 02:10 deploy this morning:

> *"Hands-on agentic AI training in Oxford for business leaders. **Next cohort 26 Nov 2026.** In one day you
> build and run an agentic AI workflow on your own task."*

**26 November is a different day for a different reader** - the Coding Bootcamp is for *"people who have not yet
shipped software"*, where *"Claude Code and Codex do the typing"*, and its deliverable is a live site and a
prototype, not a workflow against a task you already do by hand. So the one field an engine quotes most
readily, on **the one page a domain-restricted search demonstrably returns**, dated the agentic-workflow day to
the coding day and omitted **3 December** altogether. A buyer who read it and booked would be on the wrong day;
one who read it and could not make 26 November would conclude there was nothing until January.

**The fix is to the date, not to the sentences, and it is the house pattern already.** Both programme pages
pair their own date with their own promise - `/bootcamps/oxford-agentic-bootcamp/` reads *"Next cohort
3 December 2026. ... a working agentic AI workflow on a real task from your own work"* and
`/bootcamps/agentic-coding-bootcamp/` reads *"Next cohort 26 November 2026. ... have not yet shipped
software"*. The homepage was the only page pairing one line's date with another line's promise. The sentences
themselves are positioning (the message house of 13 August) and **not the loop's to rewrite**, so the date
moved instead: `upcoming[0]` became `upcoming.find(e => e.data.programme.id === 'oxford-agentic-bootcamp')`.

**Taken from the page's own `upcoming` slice, deliberately, rather than from the programme's full set.** That
keeps the invariant the original comment states - it cannot name a cohort the cards do not show. If none of the
three carded cohorts is an Agentic one, the clause empties, exactly as it already does between cohorts: **no
date is weaker than a date, and a date the page does not show would be worse than either.** Measured across the
whole known schedule, the dated branch still fits the 160-character budget at every value it can take -
**154** characters with *3 Dec 2026*, **155** with *28 Jan 2027* - so it does not silently fall back to the

### 20 Nov 2026 (02:00 cycle) - the one guide whose whole subject is when cohorts run listed six dates as one flat roster, three of them spent, with no tense on any of them. It now reads has-run and on-sale, and for the first time the sentence is visible to `check:dates`. One paragraph, one file, 4 of 209 built files

**This is the last open piece of backlog 89, and it is the piece that item said no check could see.** The
Agentic half closed last night when Cohort 3's capsule went into the past tense. What was left was
`when-ai-executive-cohorts-run`'s event roster, which backlog 89 explicitly deferred to this cycle as *"a copy
decision for the 20 November rewrite, not a retarget"*.

**The defect.** The guide's second paragraph read: *"...which is why the 2026 sequence is as uneven as it is:
the Oxford Agentic Bootcamp on **16 September** and **19 November**, the Second Brain Bootcamp on
**21 October** at the Pitt Rivers Museum, the first Coding Bootcamp on **26 November**, and a fourth agentic
day on **3 December**. The 2027 dates were set the same way, the first of them **28 January**..."* Six dates,
each a link to its own event page, and **not one verb between them**. As of this morning three of the six have
run - 16 September, 21 October and 19 November, the last of them yesterday - and three are on sale. A reader
landing on the page that answers *when do cohorts run* could not tell which was which, and neither could an
engine extracting dates from it. **This is the stale-roster failure the GEO log has now recorded eleven times
in other people's listings, published on our own site, in the one guide whose subject it is.**

**Why no check saw it, and why one does now.** `check-dates.mjs` asks which tense word *governs* a date, and
in the old sentence nothing did: no `ran`, no `runs`, no `is on`, and the only past verb (*"Ours were set that
way"*) sat outside the 90-character window. So `governingTense` returned `none` and the roster passed every
build. The rewrite gives each date a governing verb - *"The Oxford Agentic Bootcamp **ran on** 16 September and
again on 19 November, and the Second Brain Bootcamp **ran on** 21 October"*, then *"The days still on sale are
the first Coding Bootcamp, which **runs on** 26 November, a fourth agentic day on 3 December, and the first of
the 2027 dates, which **is on** 28 January"*. Past verbs on the spent dates are durable and can never go stale;
forward verbs on the live ones are deliberately **fragile**, so the guard fires the moment each passes.
**Measured, not asserted:** at `--now=2026-11-27`, the build before this change reported **6** stale dates and
this page was **not among them**; after it, **7**, and the seventh is this sentence. The page the check's own
comment calls *"exactly the page a buyer asking when the next cohort runs would land on"* is guarded at last.

**What was preserved, deliberately.** Every fact and every link. All six event links stay (backlog 89 already
established that links to passed cohorts are legitimate evidence citations, and there are seven such links
elsewhere on the site), plus `/events/` as *"the list that stays current"*. The uneven-sequence argument, the
year anchors *"the 2026 sequence"* and *"the 2027 dates"*, the Pitt Rivers and Jesus College venue facts,
*"with the room booking there still being finalised"* (still correct: `cohort-5.md` carries `confirmed: false`
on its venue), *"Worcester College holds all of the others"* (true of the four in the list; Cohort 1 was at
St Anne's and is not in it), and the September-date coincidence with the Oxford online programme all survive
word for word. **No count was written** - *"three have run, three are on sale"* was drafted and rejected,
because a number goes stale on 26 November with nothing to catch it, whereas the tense is caught.

**Measured.** 4 of 209 files in `dist` differ against a sha256 snapshot taken before the change, **none added
and none removed**: the guide page, `llms-full.txt` (which both voice agents read) and the two sitemaps.

### 17 Nov 2026 (14:00 cycle) - the 56 social cards were the last surface publishing em dashes, and the /team/ card described one bootcamp when there are three. Backlog 108, both halves, and a guard so no card can drift again

**The defect, in two parts, both found by the 09:00 cycle while fixing the stale headline in the
same file.** (a) Every card joined its eyebrow and its meta line with an **em dash** -
`The Oxford Agentic Bootcamp — Cohort 5`, `Thu, 28 January 2027 — Jesus College, Oxford` - while
the house style has none and the page behind each card writes the identical two strings with a
spaced hyphen. This was not a judgement call: `src/pages/events/[slug].astro:143` builds the same
eyebrow from the same two fields with `.join(' - ')`, `src/layouts/Base.astro:50` joins a page title
to the brand with `' - '`, and `BaseHead.astro:81` titles the RSS feed `Oxford Agentic - Guides`.
The cards disagreed with all three. The 9 November cycle removed 36 em dashes from the two files
written for machines on exactly this ground; the cards were what that sweep could not see.
(b) The `/team/` card was titled **"The people who run the day"** while the page it represents is
titled **"The people who run it"** - and that wording was chosen deliberately, because "the day"
describes one bootcamp when the site runs three.

**The fix.** Eight strings in `src/pages/og/[key].png.ts`: seven separators and the `/team/` title.
Nothing else was touched - not the comments in the same file, not the testimonial quotes in
`src/content/testimonials/`, which are four real people's own words and are not ours to restyle.

**The guard, which is the part worth keeping.** Card text is painted into a PNG by satori, so **no
check over `dist` can read it**: no grep, no link check, no schema check, no date check. That is how
a three-month-stale headline survived here until this morning and how these survived until this
afternoon. The route now asserts, at build time and on the strings themselves, that no card field
contains an en or em dash, and throws if one does. **Proved by deliberately reintroducing one**: the
build exited 1 with `og card /team/: eyebrow uses an en or em dash. House style is a spaced hyphen.`
A guard that has never been seen to fail is not a guard.

**Measured.** Blast radius **44 of 209 files in `dist`**, every one a PNG under `dist/og/`, none
added or removed. **Zero HTML pages changed**, so no page copy moved, no `updatedDate` was bumped
and no `lastmod` moved. The 44 is itself the check: 56 cards minus the 12 that never carried an em

### 17 Nov 2026 (02:00 cycle) - the Event nodes said a company runs the day and never said who. Each on-sale event now names its own facilitators as `performer`, resolving to the `Person` node its `/team/` profile already publishes - no copy changed, no new fact asserted, every event page's visible HTML byte-identical

**The defect, measured rather than assumed.** Every `EducationEvent` node on this site carried
`performer: { '@id': ORG_ID }` and nothing else. Meanwhile each on-sale event page names its
facilitators in prose, in its own "Who runs it?" answer, and the site publishes a full `Person` node
for each of them at `/team/<slug>/#person` - name, job title, bio, `worksFor`, `sameAs`. So the graph
held both halves of "who teaches this day" and joined neither: an engine reading the Event learned
that a company runs it, and an engine reading the profile learned a biography with no event attached.
The `speakers` field exists in the events schema (`z.array(reference('team'))`, `src/content.config.ts`)
and **no event file used it** - zero occurrences across all seven.

**The evidence that this costs something.** The 13 Nov 2026 (14:00) probe is the clearest instance in
the GEO log: asked how this site relates to the University of Oxford, the engine had to infer our
people from a **Luma host list**, because nothing on this site tied a named person to a named day.
This does not fix retrieval - nothing on-page has, for twenty-four cycles - but it is the one fact the
graph was missing, and it is free to assert because the page already says it in words.

**What changed.**
- `speakers` populated on the four on-sale event pages, in the order each page's own "Who runs it?"
  answer reads: Cohorts 3, 4 and 5 get Drummond Gilbert, Nicolai Thomson, Emine Gokce Phillips and
  Jonathan Waddingham; the Coding Bootcamp's Cohort 1 gets Drummond Gilbert, Jonathan Waddingham and
  Mike Bailey. **The three past events were deliberately left empty**: their pages name nobody, and a
  performer list on a page that does not name its people would be an assertion the page does not make.
- `eventSchema` takes a resolved facilitator list and emits `performer` as an array - the Organization
  first, then one `Person` per facilitator carrying `@type`, the team file's own `name`, the
  `#person` `@id` and the profile `url`. The name is read from the team file, never built from the
  slug, and nothing else about the person is restated here, so the Event node and the profile cannot
  drift.
- Guarded on `config.features.team`, for the same reason `personSchema` is: with the flag off
  `/team/` does not build, and these would be references to pages nothing serves - the exact fault the
  graph-reference rule in `check-schema.mjs` was added on 14 November to catch. Flag off, the
  Organization stands alone exactly as before, and `npm run check:flags` passes both builds.

**`updatedDate` was deliberately not bumped on the four event files, and the measurement is the
reason.** Every event page's **visible** HTML is byte-identical before and after - checked by
rebuilding at the previous commit, keeping all seven event pages, rebuilding with the change and
diffing each pair with the `ld+json` blocks removed: seven of seven identical. `updatedDate` drives
sitemap `lastmod`, and `astro.config.mjs` derives several other pages' `lastmod` from the newest event
`updatedDate` - including `/events/`, whose bytes did not change at all. Bumping it would therefore
move `lastmod` on byte-identical pages, which is the truthfulness objection **backlog 83** raises
against exactly this. The served event files did change, so this is a judgement rather than a rule;
IndexNow submits the changed URLs regardless.

### 16 Nov 2026 (14:00 cycle) - the stale-date guard's forward-verb list was literal, so one word between the verb and its preposition hid a booking-page claim from it. One regex, 0 of 209 built files changed, and the `at` version of the same fix fails this build today

**Evidence, and it is the guard's own blind spot measured rather than argued.** Backlog 102 recorded
on 15 November that `FORWARD` holds `is on` and `are on` and not `is there on`, and that the instance
which exposed it had just been rewritten away for other reasons - so the gap was "unobserved rather
than fixed". This cycle swept every long-month date window on all 58 indexable pages and resolved the
governing tense of each: **32 windows resolve to no tense at all**, which is where the guard is blind.
Thirty-one of them are safe. **Twenty** are derived cards, "next cohort" bands, stat panels, article
bylines and the `assurances` under each booking form, all of which self-heal from `effectiveStatus` on
the next build or disappear with the panel that prints them. **Eleven** are prose, and every one is
either a past fact stated in the past tense or a sentence the 15 and 16 November cycles wrote
deliberately tense-neutral so that it survives its own dates - the venue answers on `/` and the
Agentic programme page, and the 02:00 cycle's *"Ours were set that way, individually"* roster.

**The thirty-second is a live defect with a date on it.** `/bootcamps/agentic-coding-bootcamp/`, the
Coding Bootcamp's *"Where in Oxford is it held?"* answer: ***"Cohort 1 is there on Thursday
26 November 2026."*** True today, false on 27 November, and on that morning the "Upcoming runs" card
beside it has already gone, so the sentence stands alone - and the old pattern returned nothing,
because `is there on` matches neither list. A buyer opening the venue answer after the day had run
would have been told where a passed cohort *is*.

**The change.** One optional word is allowed between `is`/`are` and `on`, which also covers "is held
on" and "is also on" without enumerating adverbs, and `not` is excluded so that "is not on
16 September" denies a date rather than claiming it. `is on`/`are on` leave the literal list and
become the no-adverb case of the same alternative, so nothing is lost.

**`at` was tested and rejected, on a measurement rather than a judgement.** The obvious companion fix
is to accept `is at`/`are at` too, since Cohort 5's venue is the thing that moved this month. It
**fails this build today, on a true sentence**: the Agentic programme page's *"Cohorts 2, 3 and 4 are
all at Worcester College on Walton Street - 16 September, 19 November and 3 December 2026"*, which the
15 November cycle wrote in exactly that shape so it would stay true as each date passes. A venue fact
survives its dates; a scheduling claim does not, and `at` is how the first one is written. At later

gate, blocking a deploy on correct copy is worse than one blind spot, so the widening stops at `on`
and the reasoning is in the file next to the regex.

### 16 Nov 2026 (09:00 cycle) - the programme pages filed cohorts that have already run under a heading that says "Upcoming runs". The heading outline now closes before them, and not one pixel moved

**Evidence.** `/bootcamps/[slug]/` built its whole runs block as a single
`<section aria-labelledby="runs">` headed `<h2>Upcoming runs</h2>`, with "Previous cohorts"
inside it as an `h3` - the same level as the cohort cards themselves. The measured outline on
`/bootcamps/oxford-agentic-bootcamp/` was: **h2 Upcoming runs, h3 Cohort 3, h3 Cohort 4,
h3 Cohort 5, h3 Previous cohorts, h3 Cohort 2, h3 Cohort 1.** Every cohort sat at one level
under "Upcoming runs", and the label meant to separate them was a sibling of the things it
labels rather than their parent. Someone navigating by heading, or reading the outline, was
told that Cohort 1 (21 July 2026) and Cohort 2 (16 September 2026) are upcoming runs. Three of
the six are bookable and three are over, so this is a booking-relevant confusion, not a tidiness
one. `check-dates.mjs` cannot see it: every date on the page is correct, and the structure is
what misfiles them.

**The pattern was already in the repo, so nothing was invented.** `/events/` has always done

the past cohorts are additionally inside a region named "Previous cohorts".

property an `h2` would have changed is `line-height` (1.08 against the `h3`'s 1.2); that is now
pinned in the same rule. Checked by measuring the section box, the title box and the computed
font-size, line-height, weight, family, colour and margin at 375, 768 and 1280px, plus the full
document height of all three programme pages: **every value identical before and after**, and

before/after screenshots of the runs section are **byte-identical**.

```
a.card [aria-hidden='true'], .btn [aria-hidden='true'] { display: inline-block; ... }
```

Its own comment says "scoped to decorative arrow spans only". The selector is not: it matches any

|---|---|---|---|
| 320px | 233px | 233px | **233px** |
| 375px | **51px** | 285px | **285px** |
| 768px | **58px** | 287px | **287px** |
| 1280px | **58px** | 183px | **183px** |

(320px is in the table because it is the one width where the before was already right - the card
is narrow enough there that the two agree by accident, which is why a single-width check would
have passed it.)

**Fixed in the team component, not in `global.css`.** `a.card .person__initials { display: flex;
width: 100% }`, which Astro scopes to (0,3,1) and so wins outright. The arrow rule is doing its own
job correctly on every other card, and narrowing it would mean guessing at what counts as an arrow.

### 15 Nov 2026 (08:00 cycle) - the stale-date guard exempted a forward-tense claim whenever a true past-tense claim sat beside it, so the page whose whole subject is when cohorts run was the one page it could never flag. The governing verb now decides, and the guard gains three real instances: 0 of 203 built files changed

**The defect, measured before it was fixed, and it had a date on it.** `check-dates.mjs` hard-fails
the build when rendered copy names a passed cohort's date as still to come. It built its 90-character
window around the date, then skipped the instance if `PAST` matched **anywhere in that window**. That
reads as "something here says the day has gone", which is true of a window describing one day and
false of a window describing several - and this site has a page whose whole subject is several.
`/guides/when-ai-executive-cohorts-run/` publishes, in a single sentence:

> "in 2026 the Oxford Agentic Bootcamp **ran** on 16 September and **runs again on 19 November**, the
> Coding Bootcamp **takes** its first cohort a week after that **on 26 November**, all three at
> Worcester College, and the Second Brain Bootcamp **ran** on 21 October at the Pitt Rivers Museum."

Every clause is true today. On **20 November** the 19 November clause is false; on **27 November** so
is the 26 November one. The old rule stayed silent on both, because `ran` - which governs 16 September,
a **different cohort** - sat inside the same window and spoke for dates it does not govern. Instrumented
on the built page: for `19 November` the window matched `PAST -> "ran"` and `FORWARD -> "runs"`, and
`PAST` won by being tested first.

**So the blind spot was the page the buyer in the probe below actually lands on.** At
`--now=2026-11-20` the old rule reported **11** stale instances and this guide was not among them.

**The fix is one rule with one reason: ask which tense word GOVERNS the date, not which ones are near
it.** In prose of this shape the governing verb precedes its date - "ran on 16 September", "runs again
on 19 November", "takes its first cohort ... on 26 November", "Took place on 16 September 2026" - so
the **nearest tense word before the date wins**. Where no tense word precedes the date inside the
window, the old whole-window reading stands, and that is deliberate rather than lazy: it is what
catches the derived listings, where the marker is a bare "Upcoming" heading rows above a date, and
dropping it would lose instances that fail correctly today. `takes` was added to `FORWARD`, which is
what the 26 November clause needs and the only vocabulary change.

**Strictly additive, proved by diffing the old rule against the new at both dates. Nothing was lost;
three real prose instances were gained**, and one of the three was not predicted, which is the
evidence the rule is a tense rule rather than a fix tailored to one page:

| | 20 Nov | 27 Nov |
|---|---|---|
| old rule | 11 | 15 |
| new rule | **13** | **18** |
| lost | **0** | **0** |

- `/guides/when-ai-executive-cohorts-run/` - the targeted one, at both dates (19 November), and again
  at 27 November for 26 November.
- `/events/oxford-agentic-bootcamp-cohort-1/` - **not predicted**: *"Cohort 2 ran on Wednesday
  16 September 2026, and Cohort 3 runs on Thursday 19 November 2026."* The same shape, in prose, on a
  second page. A correct past clause about Cohort 2 was exempting a forward claim about Cohort 3.

**Proved by mutation on a throwaway copy of `dist`, and the mutation is the decisive one.** Control at
`--now=2026-11-27`: 18 instances, this guide named twice. The same tree with **only the two verbs put
into the past tense** (`runs again on` to `ran again on`, `takes its first cohort` to `took its first
cohort`), nothing else touched: **16 instances, this guide named 0 times.** The rule tracks the tense
of the governing verb, not the page.

**No false positives, which is the half that matters because this check hard-fails a deploy.** At
today's date the new rule reports **0 errors over 55 indexable pages**, identical to the old rule's
control, and the pass lines are unchanged. The regression case worth naming is the Second Brain
closers - *"Cohort 1 ran on 21 October 2026 at the Pitt Rivers Museum, and dates for the next cohort
are being confirmed"* - where `next` is a `FORWARD` word sitting **after** a past date. The nearest
word before it is `ran`, so it stays correctly exempt.

**Checks read by exit code.** `npm ci` and `npm run build` green, every figure identical to the
baseline: 66 pages, 3,247 internal links resolve, 12 Event nodes (7 top-level, 5 nested entity),
20 FAQPage, 128 offset-bearing publication dates, 1,293 resolving graph references, 56 well-formed
breadcrumb trails, `check:dates` 0 findings and 0 year-less dates. `npm run check:flags` green on both
builds. **Blast radius against a sha256 snapshot of `dist`: 0 of 203 files differ**, none added or
removed, because the only file touched is a check script the build does not import. The outbound
checker reports 0 of 11 third-party links reachable, which is this sandbox's egress policy and not a
site fault.

**Headless Chromium over four pages at 375 and 1280px: 50 assertions, 0 fail**, 0 JS exceptions, 0
failed same-origin requests, 0 horizontal overflow. The assertions are chosen for this change: each
clause the rule now reads was asserted present in the **live DOM's visible text**, and every long-month
date on those pages was checked to sit in an element that is not `display:none`, `visibility:hidden`
or zero-opacity - because a guard that reads rendered text is only as honest as the text being
rendered to a reader. Nothing moved visually, which follows from `dist` being byte-identical.

**IndexNow submits nothing, and that is the honest number.** All four changed paths are excluded by
name in `scripts/indexnow-ping.mjs` (`^(IMPROVEMENTS)\.md$`, `^outreach/`, `^seo-data/`,
`^scripts/check-[a-z-]+\.mjs$`), so `wholeSite` stays false with no page candidates and the script
takes its `no page URLs affected by this push; nothing to submit` branch. That matches the whole-`dist`
diff of 0 files, so it is not an instance of backlog 85 for once. The mapping was read rather than run:
this session's tool policy refuses the ping script even with `--dry-run`, and the deploy workflow owns
the ping regardless.

**What this buys, stated plainly.** It does not fix a word of copy. It means that on 20 November, when
Cohort 3 passes, the build stops on **13** named instances rather than 11, and the two it would have
missed are the sentence a buyer reads on the scheduling guide and the sentence on Cohort 1's page. The
same on 27 November at 18 rather than 15. The 5 November incident that caused this guard to exist - an
answer engine naming a passed 21 October date as "the next listed in-person date" - is exactly the
failure these two would have reproduced.

**The sweep this forecasts, recorded so the next cycles do not re-derive it.** From 20 November,
`/bootcamps/oxford-agentic-bootcamp/`, `/events/`, the three Agentic event pages and six guides
(`claude-cowork-claude-code-or-codex`, `getting-an-ai-bootcamp-approved`,
`getting-an-ai-workflow-past-it-and-legal`, `what-you-can-build-in-one-day-with-ai`,
`when-ai-executive-cohorts-run`, `where-the-human-goes-in-an-agentic-workflow`,
`who-should-take-the-seat`) need their Cohort 3 sentences put in the past tense. Two of those are

cohort are being confirmed."*

**GEO: four probes, zero citations, and the one that matters is a dated reach failure rather than a

### 15 Nov 2026 (02:00 cycle) - the graph reference rule proved every breadcrumb URL goes somewhere and said nothing about whether the trail is a list. One shape rule, three predicates, and the one with teeth is the one nothing could have caught: 0 of 203 built files changed

**Backlog 99, taken as scoped and with the question it said to settle first settled.** The 14 Nov
